You are doing functional research for "Atlas ERP", an open-source ERP whose explicit benchmark is SAP S/4HANA. Your assigned S/4HANA area: Quality Management & Plant Maintenance (QM / PM-EAM).

TASK: Establish what this area actually covers in current S/4HANA (2025/2026), identify the 6-12 capabilities practitioners consider essential, and judge each against the planned Atlas v1 scope below.

METHOD: Use WebSearch (and WebFetch for promising pages) - 2 to 5 targeted searches. Prefer SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, and reputable ERP consulting sources. If web tools are unavailable or consistently fail, fall back to your embedded knowledge of S/4HANA and say so explicitly in the overview field.

COVER AT MINIMUM: QM: inspection lots, inspection plans, results recording, usage decisions, quality notifications. PM/EAM: equipment and functional locations, maintenance notifications and orders, preventive maintenance plans, measurement points.

PLANNED ATLAS V1 SCOPE FOR THIS AREA (judge full/partial/out-of-scope against THIS, not your own ideas):
Inspection flag on goods receipt -> inspection lot -> accept/reject with stock disposition; equipment register; corrective and preventive (interval-based) maintenance orders. Inspection plans, usage-decision codes, functional locations and measurement points are not in the v1 list.

RULES:
- atlas_v1 = "full" when Atlas v1 plans the practitioner-essential core of the capability; "partial" when a meaningful but reduced subset is planned; "out-of-scope" when none of it is planned.
- Every "partial" and "out-of-scope" entry MUST have a non-empty reason (why cut / where the boundary sits) and later_path (how to add it later in one line).
- atlas_module must be one of: finance, inventory, procurement, sales, manufacturing, quality, maintenance, hr, projects, crm, reporting, admin, industry, core, frontend, or "-" for out-of-scope.
- Be honest: if S/4HANA has an essential capability the Atlas plan misses entirely, include it as out-of-scope rather than omitting it.

Your final output is consumed by a script - return only the structured data.

Based on the search results, here's an overview of SAP S/4HANA Quality Management's key capabilities:

## Key Capabilities of SAP S/4HANA Quality Management

### **Quality Planning**
Quality planning involves the creation and management of master data required to control how quality inspections should be conducted, including defining inspection characteristics, sampling procedures, and inspection methods.

### **Inspection Plans**
Inspection plans help define how a quality inspection of one or several materials is to take place, and for reuse purposes, you can integrate master data in your inspection plans. An inspection plan can contain several operations, which reflect the different inspection stages for the product, with work centers and production resources/tools assigned to each operation, and each operation can contain several inspection characteristics.

### **Inspection Lot and Results Recording**
When inspection lots are created, the quality technician opens the Record Inspection Results app to start from the list of inspection lots in their responsibility and enters characteristic results for each inspection to be executed. The app supports both recording of single inspection results (allowing entering individual values for quantitative or qualitative characteristics) and summarized inspection results recording (entering a single aggregated value for a characteristic).

### **Usage Decision**
The Manage Inspection Lots app enables you to record inspection results and make usage decisions for inspection lots from the worklist page.

### **Quality Notification**
Quality Notifications are used to document and process quality issues, capturing detailed information about the problem and tracking the resolution process until the issue is closed.

### **Quality Control**
Quality Control involves the statistical analysis of inspection data to monitor and improve process performance, including real-time process data visualization, creation of statistical process control charts, identification of out-of-control conditions, and performing detailed analysis to identify trends and patterns.

content.content:
# SAP S/4HANA Quality Management: Main Capabilities

Based on the guide, here are the core capabilities:

**Quality Planning:** Creation and management of inspection master data, including inspection characteristics, sampling procedures, and inspection methods with dynamic modification rules.

**Quality Inspection:** Conducting actual product inspections at various touchpoints—vendor receipt, pre-shipment, manufacturing, or equipment maintenance—with result recording and follow-up actions.

**Quality Notifications:** Documentation of quality issues "reported by customers, issues identified with vendors, or internal problems," tracking resolution until closure.

**Quality Certificates:** Proof of compliance with quality requirements, issued to customers or requested from suppliers to verify standards are met.

**Audit Management:** Planning and executing audits with checklist definitions, finding capture, and corrective/preventive action tracking.

**Test Equipment Management:** Management of testing equipment information with "routine calibrations and maintenance" scheduling to ensure accuracy and regulatory compliance.

**Quality Control:** Statistical analysis of inspection data enabling "real-time process data visualization, creation of statistical process control charts," trend identification, and out-of-control detection.

**Non-Conformance & CAPA:** Documentation of problems, root cause investigation, corrective action implementation, and effectiveness monitoring.

**Supplier Quality Management:** Tracking vendor performance, managing quality levels for supplied materials, handling certificates, and managing non-compliant material returns.

# SAP S/4HANA Plant Maintenance Capabilities

Based on the article provided, the following core PM/asset management capabilities are discussed:

**Work Order Management**
The article highlights the "Manage Work Order" Fiori app, which allows maintenance planners to access information with fewer clicks, "reducing the planning cycle time by up to 25%."

**Maintenance Notifications & Planning**
The system supports notifications and planning processes, though specific details about the notification workflow aren't extensively covered in this content.

**Real-Time Data & Analytics**
S/4HANA enables continuous tracking of key performance indicators such as Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) and Mean Time to Repair (MTTR), moving beyond overnight batch processing for equipment status visibility.

**Predictive Maintenance Integration**
The platform integrates with tools like SAP Predictive Asset Insights, which uses "IoT sensors, historical performance data, and machine learning to predict failures before they happen."

**Simplified Data Architecture**
The system consolidates maintenance history, asset performance data, and cost controls into "a unified view," improving decision-making speed and cost control.

**Mobile Access**
SAP Fiori apps provide "mobile-friendly interfaces" for maintenance technicians and planners.

The article doesn't provide detailed descriptions of specific technical objects, BOMs, measurement points, counters, or formal task list structures.

input.overview: In current S/4HANA (2025/2026), QM covers quality planning (inspection plans, master inspection characteristics, sampling), quality inspection (inspection lots auto-created at goods receipt, in production, and at delivery), characteristic-level results recording, coded usage decisions that drive stock postings out of quality-inspection stock, and quality notifications/CAPA, plus certificates and supplier quality. PM-EAM (Asset Management) centers on technical objects (equipment installed on hierarchical functional locations), maintenance notifications feeding corrective maintenance orders with a phase-based lifecycle, preventive maintenance plans (time-, performance/counter-, and strategy-based) scheduled against task lists, and measurement points/counters for condition readings; the 2025 release adds enhanced Fiori order management, scheduling, and analytics. Findings are based on live web research (SAP Learning Journey, SAP Help Portal listing, ERP Research module guide, ASUG and NRX analyses of the 2025 release) supplemented by embedded S/4HANA knowledge where pages could not be fetched (SAP Help body content and one SAP Community post returned errors). Against the Atlas v1 plan, the GR-inspection-to-disposition flow, equipment register, and corrective/interval-based preventive orders cover a credible minimal core, but inspection plans, results recording, quality and maintenance notifications, functional locations, and measurement points are genuine gaps practitioners will notice.

capabilities.description: System-created inspection objects (from goods receipt, production, deliveries, or manual) that hold stock in quality inspection until decided
capabilities.reason: Only GR-origin lots via an inspection flag are planned; production/in-process, delivery, and manual lot origins plus sampling/sample-size logic are not
capabilities.later_path: Extend the existing lot object with additional origins (production order, delivery, manual) and sampling procedures

capabilities.capability: Inspection plans and master inspection characteristics
capabilities.description: Reusable task-list master data defining operations, characteristics, sampling procedures, and inspection methods per material
capabilities.reason: Explicitly excluded from the v1 list; v1 lots are plan-less binary accept/reject with no characteristic or sampling master data
capabilities.later_path: Introduce inspection plan + characteristic master data and assign plans to lots at creation

capabilities.description: Recording quantitative/qualitative results per inspection characteristic (single or summarized) with automatic valuation against tolerances
capabilities.reason: Depends on inspection plans/characteristics, which are cut; v1 captures only a lot-level accept/reject outcome, not measured values
capabilities.later_path: After plans/characteristics exist, add a characteristic-level results entry screen with auto-valuation

capabilities.description: Coded decision (UD catalog) closing the lot and posting quantities to unrestricted, blocked, scrap, sample, or return-to-vendor stock
capabilities.reason: Binary accept/reject with a stock move is planned, but coded UD catalogs, quality scores, and split-quantity postings (scrap/sample/return) are not
capabilities.later_path: Add UD code catalogs and multi-bucket quantity split posting on top of the existing accept/reject action

capabilities.description: Structured records of internal defects, supplier complaints, and customer complaints with tasks, causes, and corrective actions tracked to closure
capabilities.reason: No defect/complaint workflow in v1; a rejected lot only moves stock and does not open a tracked quality issue
capabilities.later_path: Add a generic notification/issue object (shared with maintenance notifications) linkable to lots, suppliers, and materials

capabilities.description: Certificates of analysis issued to customers or required from suppliers; quality info records gating procurement by vendor quality status
capabilities.reason: Not in the v1 plan; mainly needed in regulated industries and dependent on results recording, which is also cut
capabilities.later_path: Generate certificate documents from recorded results and add a vendor-material quality status check in procurement

capabilities.description: Equipment master records installed on hierarchical functional locations, carrying maintenance history, criticality, and structure
capabilities.reason: A flat equipment register is planned, but functional-location hierarchies, install/dismantle, and structure-based reporting are explicitly excluded
capabilities.later_path: Add a functional location entity with hierarchy codes and equipment installation/dismantle links

capabilities.description: Malfunction reports, activity reports, and maintenance requests that document problems and convert into maintenance orders
capabilities.reason: v1 creates corrective orders directly with no notification/request stage, losing breakdown reporting and MTBF/MTTR-style analysis
capabilities.later_path: Add a lightweight notification object convertible to an order, reusing the shared notification model

capabilities.description: Work orders against equipment with planning, execution, status lifecycle, completion, and cost capture (phase-based in current releases)
Time-based, performance/counter-based, and strategy plans whose scheduling automatically generates maintenance calls (orders/notifications)
capabilities.reason: Only fixed interval-based (time) preventive orders are planned; counter/performance-based and strategy plans are impossible without measurement points
capabilities.later_path: Once counters exist, extend the scheduler with performance-based cycles and packaged strategy plans

capabilities.description: Condition readings and usage counters on technical objects, documented as measurement documents and used to trigger maintenance
capabilities.reason: Explicitly excluded from the v1 list; no condition readings or counter-driven triggers are planned
capabilities.later_path: Add a measuring point entity on equipment with reading documents that feed maintenance plan scheduling

capabilities.description: Reusable operation lists (general, equipment, functional-location task lists) assigned to maintenance items and orders to standardize work
capabilities.reason: Not in the v1 plan; v1 preventive/corrective orders would carry free-text work instead of reusable standardized operations
capabilities.later_path: Add a task list master assignable to maintenance plan items and copyable into orders

content.text: Research complete. Structured output delivered with 12 capabilities across QM and PM-EAM judged against the Atlas v1 scope.
